about_disclaimerP: No More Room in Hell 2 Wiki is a fan-made, community-maintained resource. We are not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Torn Banner Studios.
about_gameP1: No More Room in Hell 2 is a first-person cooperative zombie survival shooter from Torn Banner Studios, the team behind the original No More Room in Hell and Chivalry. Up to eight players drop into zombie-infested locations across the American Northeast Coast as volunteer Responders, completing missions for the Civil Recovery Corps while scavenging gear and fighting for their lives.
about_gameP2: Every run is high-stakes — a single infection can turn your character against the squad, and true permadeath means a fallen Responder is gone for good. Between deployments you invest Credits earned from extracted supplies into new skills, loadouts and cosmetic upgrades back at your campsite. The Armageddon 1.0 update launched the game on consoles with Survival mode, solo play and the new Raven Rock map.

about_wikiP1: No More Room in Hell 2 Wiki is built by the community, for the community. Every guide, weapon review, map walkthrough and tier ranking is written by players who actually deploy, so the advice reflects how the game plays in real squads — not just how it appears in marketing screenshots.
about_wikiP2: Because Torn Banner Studios pushes major balance patches every few weeks, our editors regularly revisit guides, weapon reviews and tier lists after each Armageddon update. If you spot outdated information, join the Discord and let the community know so we can keep the wiki accurate.
category_advantages_guides: The guides category gives new Responders a clear, ordered path from the campsite loading screen to running full Nightmare extractions with a coordinated squad. Every guide is built around the actual in-game mechanics — control bindings, infection stages, scavenging priorities — rather than generic zombie-shooter advice. Because the game has multiple roles and overlapping systems (Responder management, loadout building, perk selection, map knowledge), the guides break each one into digestible steps with screenshots and callouts so you can read what you need in the lobby. The category also answers the practical questions players search for, such as how to heal teammates, how to barricade a doorway, how to call extraction, and how to avoid the most common causes of permadeath. Whether you are learning the controls on PC or revisiting tactics after the 1.0 Armageddon update, this is the most reliable starting point on the wiki.
category_advantages_maps: The maps category gives every Responder a detailed pre-deployment briefing for every official map so you always know the loot hotspots, defensive positions and extraction routes before you drop in. Each map article covers spawn points, key objectives, ambush wave triggers, defensive chokepoints and the best extraction timing, drawn from real co-op and solo clears. The category also highlights hidden loot rooms, secret side paths and rare spawn locations so experienced players can find the gene therapy vial or extra ammo crates that turn a losing run into a successful exfil. Because the 1.0 Armageddon update added Raven Rock, Flooded, Lighthouse and Night of the Living Dead, this category also includes the new maps so you have the latest intel for the latest content.
category_advantages_multiplayer: The multiplayer category gives every player a complete guide to playing No More Room in Hell 2 with friends, including crossplay setup, lobby management, voice chat etiquette and dedicated server options. Each article breaks down the specific feature (crossplay, proximity voice, matchmaking) with screenshots and step-by-step instructions so even a brand-new console player can squad up with their PC friends. The category also covers performance optimisation — how to fix lag spikes, how to switch server regions for lower ping, and how to troubleshoot the most common connection errors. Whether you are setting up your first crossplay session or optimising your ping for a Nightmare run, this is the most reliable multiplayer reference on the wiki.
category_advantages_responders: The responders category gives every player a complete guide to managing their three-slot roster so a single bad run does not destroy your progression. Each Responder management article covers loadout building, perk selection, cosmetic unlocks and roster rotation, with concrete recommendations for Main, Experiment and Backup slots. The category also explains how Credits and Merits interact, how the rescue beacon works in combat, and how to unlock new backgrounds and outfits without spending real money. Whether you are creating your first Responder or rebuilding after a permadeath wipe, this is the most reliable roster-management reference on the wiki.
category_advantages_skills: The skills category gives every Responder a deep, numbers-driven understanding of the entire perk tree so you can build a loadout that matches your playstyle. Each perk article includes the base value, the Expert-tier value, the unlock cost and the best build partners, drawn from the latest Armageddon 1.0 balance pass. The meta-build guides then combine perks into named archetypes (Tank, Medic, Scout, Ammo Mule) so you can copy a proven build rather than experimenting from scratch. Because each perk has unique strengths, the category highlights underused picks like the Deprived perk (extra XP from kills, ideal for grinding) and the Wicked perk (massive headshot damage boost), giving experienced players reasons to experiment beyond the meta.
category_advantages_survival: The survival category gives every Responder a complete understanding of the two systems that define the game — NPV infection and permadeath. Each infection stage article explains the symptoms, the timer length and the recommended response, so you know exactly what to do when you hear the first cough or see the first hallucination. The phalanx pill and gene therapy guides break down spawn locations, stack rules and timing windows so your squad never wastes a dose. The permadeath guides explain how to manage a three-Responder roster, when to extract early, and how to spread risk across multiple characters so a single bad run does not destroy your entire progression.

Each tier includes the criteria used (damage, reliability, versatility) and the specific scenarios where the weapon shines. The category also highlights underused picks (Rochester 1873 for headshot players, hatchet for stealth) so experienced players have reasons to experiment beyond the meta. Because the list is updated after every major balance patch, you can trust that the rankings reflect the current Armageddon 1.0 values rather than launch-day guesses.

The category also includes analysis of how each patch affects existing builds — which perks got buffed, which weapons got nerfed, which zombie types became more dangerous. category_faq_guides_a_0: Buy the game on Steam, PS5 or Xbox, then create your first Responder at the campsite and pick a loadout that includes a melee weapon, a sidearm, one medkit and a single primary firearm. Join a public lobby, deploy into Lewiston (the easiest Objective map), and follow your squad rather than running off alone. Read the beginner guide before your first deployment so you understand the infection meter, the extraction system and the rules of permadeath before you risk your first character.
category_faq_guides_a_1: When a Responder's health reaches zero, or when the NPV infection meter reaches 100% and they fully convert into a zombie, that character is permanently deleted from your roster. Any unspent XP, Credits and gear equipped on that Responder are lost. This is why the campsite allows you to manage up to three Responders at once — you always have a backup — and why experienced players often keep one Responder parked at low progression for risky experiments.
category_faq_guides_a_2: Yes — the 1.0 Armageddon update added a Solo mode that fills your squad with AI-controlled Responders so you can experience the full campaign without a full eight-player team. Solo mode is harder than co-op because the AI is conservative, but it is a great way to learn the maps and weapons before joining a public lobby. Crossplay also lets you mix platforms, so you can drop into a PC server from a console or vice versa.
category_faq_guides_a_3: Objective mode drops you into a map with a sequence of scripted mission goals — escort a VIP, restore power, clear a hospital — and ends when you complete them and extract. Survival mode drops you into one of three defense maps (Flooded, Lighthouse, Night of the Living Dead) and tasks your squad with surviving escalating waves for as long as possible. Survival rewards are based on wave count and are great for grinding Credits quickly.

category_faq_maps_a_0: Lewiston is the easiest Objective map and the recommended first deployment for new Responders. The map has clear linear objectives, generous loot spawns and short distances between objectives, so even a disorganised squad can complete it on Normal difficulty in under 30 minutes. Broadway is the next step up — denser interiors and more zombies, but still forgiving enough for a beginner squad.
category_faq_maps_a_1: Raven Rock and Night of the Living Dead are the hardest maps in the current roster. Raven Rock is a military bunker with narrow corridors that funnel Runners into your squad, while Night of the Living Dead is a Survival map that escalates wave density and zombie types faster than any other map. Both demand a full squad of eight veterans with coordinated voice chat.
category_faq_maps_a_2: The gene therapy vial spawns in a fixed location on every map, but the exact location varies between deployments, so you need to scout for it once you arrive. The vial looks like a small medical syringe and is usually found in a medical cabinet, a doctor bag or a hidden side room. Always have one squadmate dedicated to searching while the others hold chokepoints.

category_intro_guides: No More Room in Hell 2 is an 8-player cooperative zombie survival shooter where every deployment can be your last. Before you head out of the campsite for the first time you need to understand the core survivor loop — spawn into a map, scavenge for supplies, complete mission objectives, and extract before the horde or NPV infection overwhelms your Responder. Every action in the field costs time and ammunition, so a coordinated squad with clear roles (point, flank, support) will always outperform eight players running solo. The guides below walk you through your first deployment, then deepen into looting, inventory management, melee and firearm combat, and the extraction tactics that separate a successful exfil from a permadeath wipe. Whether you are new to the apocalypse or returning for the 1.0 Armageddon update, treat these guides as your pre-deployment checklist before every drop.
category_intro_maps: No More Room in Hell 2 features nine official maps spanning the American Northeast Coast, each with unique objectives, loot layouts, defensive chokepoints and extraction paths. The Objective maps include Lewiston (the urban Maine opener), Broadway (a New York city center with dense interiors), Powerplant (industrial Pennsylvania), Beaulieu Hospital, Raven Rock (the new 1.0 Armageddon military bunker map) and more. The Survival maps — Flooded, Lighthouse and Night of the Living Dead — task your squad with surviving escalating waves in fixed defensive setups. Every map rewards different playstyles: Lewiston teaches the basics, Raven Rock punishes loose squads, and the Survival maps are perfect for grinding Credits with a coordinated team. The articles in this category break down every official map's loot hotspots, defensive positions, ambush spots and extraction routes so you can deploy with confidence.
category_intro_multiplayer: No More Room in Hell 2 is built around 8-player cooperative play, with full crossplay across PC (Steam and Epic), PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The multiplayer experience includes party lobbies, proximity voice chat, matchmaking on dedicated servers and a recent Oceanic server added for Australian and New Zealand players. Squads work best with clear role assignments — point, flank, support, medic — and the proximity voice chat system rewards teams that stick together. Solo mode is also available after the 1.0 Armageddon update, but the game is designed around coordinated squad play. The articles in this category explain how to set up crossplay, how to manage your squad lobby, how to optimise network performance, and how to troubleshoot the most common connection issues.
category_intro_responders: Responders are the playable characters in No More Room in Hell 2 — volunteer members of the Civil Recovery Corps who deploy into zombie-infested locations to complete missions. Every player can manage up to three Responders at a time, each with their own background, starting skills, loadout inventory and cosmetic unlocks. Between deployments you spend Credits earned from extracted Supplies on new weapons, medkits, the rescue beacon and other gear, plus skill points that unlock the perk tree. Outfits, flashlights and compasses are pure cosmetics that you unlock with Credits or weekly Merits. The campsite menu is the hub for all Responder management — creating new characters, equipping loadouts, switching active Responders, and reviewing progression across your roster. The articles in this category explain every aspect of Responder management so you can build a roster that survives the apocalypse.
category_intro_skills: The skill system in No More Room in Hell 2 lets you customise every Responder with a deep perk tree that branches into survival, combat, utility and movement specialisations. Each perk has an unlock condition (Credits or character level), a base effect and an Expert-tier upgrade that further amplifies the perk for high-level players. The survival perks — Acquired Immunity, Resident Genes, Lucky Pathogen — modify how NPV infection affects your Responder. The combat perks — Butcher, Wicked, Foreman, Guts — improve damage, stability and kill effects. The utility perks — Scavenger, Caravan, Mule, Deprived — improve loot, carry weight and economy. The movement perks — Marathon Runner, Rush — improve stamina and sprint duration. Choosing the right perk combination for your build is essential for tackling Nightmare difficulty, and the articles in this category break down every perk with values, unlock conditions and meta builds.
category_intro_survival: Survival in No More Room in Hell 2 is defined by two interlocking systems — NPV infection and permanent character death. The infection meter fills every time a zombie grabs, bites or vomits on your Responder, and once it reaches 100% your character fully converts into a zombie and is lost forever. Phalanx pills slow the infection timer by hours of in-game time, while a single gene therapy vial per match can fully cure an infected Responder and grant immunity for the rest of the deployment. The permadeath system then takes that infected or downed Responder and deletes them from your roster, taking any unspent XP or credits with them. Understanding how these two systems interact is the difference between a long-running Nightmare roster and a graveyard of converted characters. The articles in this category explain every infection stage, every cure mechanic, and every permadeath trigger so you can plan around them.

A-tier weapons like the M1911 pistol, Rochester 1873 revolver and sledgehammer are strong picks with manageable tradeoffs. B-tier weapons like the M9A3, X12 shotgun and hatchet are situational solid choices for niche loadouts. C-tier weapons like the Gruber 922 and improvised melee are situational or outclassed stopgaps. The tier list is updated after every major balance patch, and every entry includes the specific scenarios where the weapon shines (or struggles) so you can match the right gun to your mission.

The roster spans handguns like the M1911 and Gruber 922, shotguns like the Fierra DB12 and X12 pump-action, rifles and SMGs such as the M7A1 carbine and MP5, plus a full melee family from the crowbar to the sledgehammer. The base Walker is the slow shambling horde you will encounter in every map, but the game also throws sprinting Runners, leaping Crawlers, gas-spewing Shamblers and armored SWAT and National Guard specials into the mix. Each variant reacts differently to weapons — Runners die to headshots but absorb body shots, while armored specials require armor-piercing rifles or shotgun slugs to put down quickly. Understanding the full zombie roster is essential for any Responder who wants to survive Nightmare difficulty, because killing the wrong zombie the wrong way is the fastest way to lose a mission. The articles in this category break down every variant with health values, weaknesses, kill priorities and spawn behaviour so you always know what you are fighting.
category_mechanics_guides: The core loop of No More Room in Hell 2 is deceptively simple but punishing in execution. You spawn at the campsite as one of up to three Responders, spend Credits on a loadout (primary, sidearm, melee, medkit, throwable), then deploy into one of nine maps in either Objective or Survival mode. While on a deployment you scavenge buildings and containers for Supplies, complete context-sensitive mission goals, manage your ammo and carry weight, and keep an eye on your infection meter. The reactive AI director is constantly spawning zombies based on noise, flashlight use and movement, so silent play and aim discipline matter as much as raw DPS. When you reach the extraction zone or call for early exfil, your carried Supplies convert into Credits and character XP back at the campsite. Between deployments you spend those Credits on skills, new weapons, outfits and additional Responder slots.
category_mechanics_maps: Each map in No More Room in Hell 2 is hand-crafted with specific objectives, ambush spawn points and extraction routes. Objective maps spawn you with a loadout and a sequence of scripted goals — escort a VIP, restore power, clear a hospital wing — and your squad must complete them in order while surviving the reactive horde. Survival maps drop you into a fixed defensive setup and task your squad with surviving escalating waves for as long as possible, with rewards scaling by wave count. Every map also has unique environmental hazards — Powerplant has moving machinery, Raven Rock has gas-filled corridors, Beaulieu Hospital has collapsing walls — that reward map knowledge over raw DPS. Extraction happens at a fixed zone on Objective maps (with an optional early-exfil radio call) and at the end of each Survival wave.
category_mechanics_multiplayer: The multiplayer system in No More Room in Hell 2 supports up to 8 players per match across all platforms via crossplay. Players can queue into public matchmaking, create friends-only private lobbies, or join dedicated community servers hosted in regions including North America, Europe, Asia and Oceania. Squad proximity voice chat is built into the game client — voice transmission fades with distance, so staying close to your teammates is rewarded. Solo mode fills your squad with AI-controlled Responders who follow basic orders but do not have the situational awareness of human players. Party lobbies let a group of friends deploy together regardless of platform, and the game automatically syncs loadouts so everyone arrives with the correct gear.
category_mechanics_responders: The Responder system is built around three slots per player account, each holding a fully-independent character with its own background, perks, loadout and cosmetic unlocks. When you deploy, you pick one Responder from your roster and head into the map with whatever loadout you have configured at the campsite. Between deployments you spend Credits (earned from extracted Supplies) on new weapons, attachments, medkits and skill points, while Merits (earned from weekly Assignments) unlock premium cosmetics. Permadeath means a lost Responder is gone forever, so experienced players always rotate their three slots between high-progression mains, experimental alts and low-risk backups. The campsite menu is also where you swap backgrounds, change outfits and manage your rescue beacon consumables.
category_mechanics_skills: The skill system is divided into four perk families — Survival, Combat, Utility and Movement — each containing multiple perks that unlock with Credits or character level. Each perk has a base effect that is active as soon as you unlock it, plus an Expert-tier upgrade that requires additional Credits and a minimum character level. The Survival perks modify how NPV infection progresses (Acquired Immunity slows the timer, Resident Genes boosts the gene therapy cure chance, Lucky Pathogen improves the chance of finding extra pills). Combat perks improve weapon handling (Butcher boosts melee damage, Wicked boosts headshot damage, Foreman improves reload speed, Guts gives health regen on kill). Utility perks improve economy (Scavenger improves loot quality, Caravan improves Supplies conversion, Mule increases carry weight, Deprived boosts XP from kills). Movement perks improve stamina (Marathon Runner extends sprint, Rush gives a short burst of speed after a melee kill).
category_mechanics_survival: The NPV infection mechanic works on a hidden timer that fills every time a zombie successfully attacks your Responder. Early symptoms are subtle — a faint cough sound effect and a barely-visible meter on the HUD — but as the meter fills the symptoms escalate into acute psychosis (visual hallucinations, screen shake, audio distortion) and finally black veins spreading across your character's arms. Each stage has a fixed in-game duration, so a single zombie bite can turn into a fully-converted Responder in under ten minutes if left untreated. Phalanx pills reset the timer and provide hours of buffer, but the only true cure is the gene therapy vial — a rare item that spawns in a fixed (but randomised) location on every map. The permadeath system then activates when a Responder dies from any cause — infection conversion, health depletion, fall damage — and the character is permanently deleted from your roster, taking any unbanked Credits and XP with them.
category_mechanics_tier-list: The tier list ranks weapons on three criteria: damage output (per-shot damage times shots-to-kill), reliability (recoil, ammo weight, accuracy) and versatility (close-range, medium-range, anti-armour). S-tier weapons excel on all three criteria — the Fierra DB12 one-shots Walkers at close range and penetrates SWAT armor, the M7A1 carbine lands two-tap headshots at medium range with controllable recoil, the sledgehammer one-shots every zombie type including armored specials. A-tier weapons excel on two criteria — the M1911 is reliable and ammo-efficient but lower damage per shot, the Rochester 1873 has high single-tap damage but slow follow-up. B-tier weapons are situational — the M9A3 is accurate but lacks the M1911's damage, the hatchet is silent but weak against armor. C-tier weapons are outclassed or limited — the Gruber 922 is fine for early game but quickly replaced, improvised melee is fine for stealth but unreliable.
category_mechanics_updates: No More Room in Hell 2 has been continuously updated since its Early Access launch on October 22 2024, with Torn Banner Studios publishing a steady stream of content drops and balance patches. The biggest single update was the 1.0 Armageddon release on August 11 2026, which launched the full game on PC plus PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S for the first time. That update introduced Survival mode with three new maps (Flooded, Lighthouse and Night of the Living Dead), the Raven Rock Objective map, Solo mode, the Tutorial, platform achievements, the new Merits currency and weekly Assignments. Between major content drops, the studio publishes weekly or bi-weekly balance patches that tweak weapon damage, perk values and zombie behaviour. category_mechanics_weapons: Every firearm in No More Room in Hell 2 has a damage profile, a recoil pattern, an ammo type, a magazine size, a reload speed and an attachment compatibility list. Damage is split into base damage and penetration — most rifles penetrate light armor, but only the Fierra DB12 shotgun and the M7A1 carbine reliably punch through SWAT and National Guard zombies. Recoil affects how quickly you can land follow-up shots; high-recoil weapons like the Rochester 1873 revolver reward single-tap aim, while low-recoil SMGs like the MP5 are excellent for sustained close fire. Ammo weight directly impacts your carrying capacity — a full stack of rifle rounds weighs almost twice as much as the same number of handgun rounds, so you cannot bring every gun to every map. Attachments like suppressors reduce noise (fewer horde spawns), optics add zoom for medium range, and extended magazines trade reload speed for sustained fire.
category_mechanics_zombies: Every zombie in No More Room in Hell 2 is driven by the AI director, which spawns additional enemies based on noise (gunfire, running, melee impacts, flashlights), squad visibility and the map's current wave state. Walkers are the basic fodder and will keep shambling towards the squad unless distracted by gunfire or flares. Runners sprint in short bursts and can leap over low obstacles, making them dangerous in narrow corridors where they can flank the squad from behind. Crawlers are dismembered Runners — they have lost their legs and crawl on the floor, but they can still grab and infect you from below, so always stomp them or finish them quickly with a melee weapon. Shamblers are slow but emit a scream that calls additional Runners, plus a toxic gas cloud that damages anyone nearby. Prime Runners and armored SWAT or National Guard variants have huge health pools and absorb rifle rounds unless you aim for the head or use armor-piercing ammo.
category_qt_guides_0: Always read the beginner guide before your first deployment. Knowing what the HUD symbols mean and how the permadeath system works will save you from losing a character in your first ten minutes. Spend five minutes learning the controls and infection meter in a quiet Lewiston lobby before attempting the harder maps — that preparation pays off across every run you do afterwards.
category_qt_guides_1: Stick with your squad. No More Room in Hell 2 punishes lone wolves with ambush waves and swarming runners, and proximity voice chat only works when teammates are within earshot. Stay within 20 metres of at least one squadmate during scavenging so the AI director spawns fewer zombies, and only split up when one player is holding a chokepoint or scouting a route for the gene therapy vial.
category_qt_guides_2: Pop phalanx pills at the first cough, not the third. Each bottle holds three doses and the timer resets every time you take one, so delaying is the single biggest mistake new Responders make. If you have a teammate who is already at the black-vein stage, you need both phalanx pills and a gene therapy vial within the next 90 seconds or they are gone for good.
category_qt_maps_0: Always scout the map before committing to an objective route. No More Room in Hell 2 rewards players who spend the first two minutes of a deployment exploring side rooms and identifying extraction paths rather than rushing to the first objective marker. Knowing where the medkits, ammo crates and gene therapy vial can spawn saves your squad hundreds of rounds of scavenging later.
category_qt_maps_1: Hold chokepoints, not rooms. On every Objective map there are narrow corridors and doorways where two players can hold off an entire Runner wave. Identify those chokepoints before the first horde spawns and rotate your squad through them rather than fighting in open courtyards where Runners can flank from three sides at once.
category_qt_maps_2: Call extraction early on Nightmare. Successful early extraction banks your Supplies for Credits and saves your Responder's progression, while waiting for the last objective on Nightmare often ends in a wipe. If your squad is wounded or low on ammo after the second objective, call early exfil and bank your progress — a partial Credits payout is better than a permadeath wipe.
category_qt_multiplayer_0: Always use proximity voice chat to coordinate. The built-in voice system is proximity-based for a reason — staying within earshot of your squadmates is the most reliable way to call out Runner flanks, share ammo and coordinate extraction. Lone wolves who wander off lose both the voice channel and the AI director's reduced horde spawns.
category_qt_multiplayer_1: Pick the closest server region. The game now offers dedicated servers in North America, Europe, Asia and Oceania, so always pick the region closest to your physical location for the lowest ping. Australian and New Zealand players should specifically pick the Oceanic server, which was added recently to address the long-standing high-ping complaints.
category_qt_multiplayer_2: Use Discord for sensitive comms. The built-in voice chat picks up ambient noise and lacks push-to-talk controls, so for serious Nightmare squads it is often better to use Discord alongside the in-game voice. The in-game voice handles proximity, the Discord handles squad-wide coordination.
category_qt_responders_0: Always keep three Responders active. The single biggest mistake new players make is leaving their second and third slots empty, which means a single permadeath wipe leaves them with no character to deploy. Create all three slots at the campsite on day one and rotate between them so you always have a backup ready.
category_qt_responders_1: Park your Backup slot at low progression. The third Responder slot is your safety net — keep them at level one with a basic loadout so you never risk losing valuable gear in a wipe. Only deploy the Backup when both Main slots are dead or when you are testing a brand-new map that you do not trust.
category_qt_responders_2: Spend Credits on skills before cosmetics. The campsite shop tempts you with outfits and emotes, but the permanent power boost from new perks and loadout slots will save your run more often than a flashy jacket. Unlock the skill tree you need for your build first, then return to cosmetics once your roster is stable.
category_qt_skills_0: Always unlock Acquired Immunity before any other perk. Infection is the single biggest cause of permadeath in No More Room in Hell 2, and the Acquired Immunity perk extends your survival window by hours of in-game time. Every build, from solo stealth to squad tank, benefits from this perk, so spend your first Credits here.
category_qt_skills_1: Pick one perk family and max it out before branching. Each perk family (Survival, Combat, Utility, Movement) has internal synergies that reward focused investment, and the Expert-tier bonuses only kick in once you have unlocked multiple perks in the same family. Spread your Credits too thin and you will never reach the Expert tier on any single perk.
category_qt_skills_2: Match your perks to your squad role. If you are the squad's ammo mule, invest in Mule and Caravan. If you are the front-line tank, invest in Guts and Butcher. If you are the scout, invest in Marathon Runner and Wicked. The strongest perk for one role can be useless for another, so always plan around your squad composition.
category_qt_survival_0: Pop phalanx pills at the first cough, not the third. Each bottle holds three doses and the timer resets every time you take one, so delaying is the single biggest mistake new Responders make. If you have a teammate who is already at the black-vein stage, you need both phalanx pills and a gene therapy vial within the next 90 seconds or they are gone for good.
category_qt_survival_1: Spread progression across all three Responder slots. No More Room in Hell 2 punishes players who load every skill point and rare weapon onto a single character, because that character can be lost to permadeath in a single bad run. Keep one slot for high-risk experiments, one for steady progression, and one parked at low level for backup extractions.
category_qt_survival_2: Call early extraction on Nightmare when infection spreads. If two squadmates are coughing and the gene therapy vial is nowhere in sight, do not gamble the entire roster on a miracle find. Call early exfil, bank the Credits you have, and reset — a partial payout is always better than losing three Responders to a single wave.
category_qt_tier-list_0: Pair one S-tier primary with one A-tier sidearm and one A-tier melee. This combination gives you the best of every range — the S-tier primary for medium and long engagements, the sidearm for backup and the melee for silent close-quarters work. Avoid the temptation to bring three S-tier weapons, because ammo weight and noise will drain your Supplies faster than you think.
category_qt_tier-list_1: Match the tier to the squad role. The strongest S-tier pick for a front-line tank is the sledgehammer or fire axe, while the strongest S-tier pick for a scout is the M7A1 carbine with a suppressor. The strongest S-tier pick for an ammo mule is irrelevant — your role is to carry Supplies, not to deal damage.
category_qt_tier-list_2: Re-evaluate the tier list after every patch. The 1.0 Armageddon update rebalanced the Gruber 922, X12 shotgun and several melee weapons, so any tier list from launch day is already out of date. Check the patch notes in the updates category before committing Credits to an expensive S-tier loadout.
category_qt_updates_0: Always check the patch notes before your first deployment after an update. The 1.0 Armageddon update rebalanced several weapons and perks, so a loadout that worked perfectly yesterday may underperform today. The patch notes section in this category is the fastest way to see what changed and adjust your build accordingly.
category_qt_updates_1: Track weekly Assignments for free Merits. The 1.0 Armageddon update added weekly Assignments that reward Merits — the premium currency for cosmetics and select loadout items. Logging in once a week to clear your Assignments is the fastest way to build a cosmetics collection without spending real money.
category_qt_updates_2: Keep an eye on the Roadmap. Torn Banner Studios publishes a public roadmap of upcoming content and balance changes, so check the official Discord or news page before planning your long-term progression. Major updates like new maps or perk reworks can change the meta overnight.
category_qt_weapons_0: Carry at least one melee weapon even on firearm-focused runs. A sledgehammer or fire axe lets you finish off crawlers silently, save ammo for the next horde, and clear interior rooms without alerting the AI director. Pair your melee with a handgun so you always have a reliable backup if your primary runs dry mid-fight.
category_qt_weapons_1: Bring the right ammo type for the mission. Rifle rounds and shotgun shells weigh more than handgun rounds, so packing three rifle mags and a full shotgun loadout will eat into your Supplies cap. Pick one primary, one sidearm and one melee unless you are running a dedicated ammo mule with the Mule perk.
category_qt_weapons_2: Reload after every fight, not during. No More Room in Hell 2 punishes reload-while-surrounded play — a long reload animation leaves you vulnerable to runner flanks. Wait for the horde to thin out, find cover, and then reload so you are ready for the next push instead of stuck with an empty mag.
category_qt_zombies_0: Always prioritise Shamblers and Prime Runners before they can summon more zombies or charge into your squad. One well-placed shotgun slug to a Shambler's head is worth more than ten shots at the surrounding Walkers, because killing the summoner drops the incoming wave count dramatically and saves your squad hundreds of rounds of follow-up fire.
category_qt_zombies_1: Listen for the cough. An infected squadmate will cough periodically as the NPV infection progresses, and that audio cue is your reminder to either find a phalanx pill bottle or start looking for the gene therapy vial location. Popping a phalanx pill at the first cough resets the timer, but waiting until the black-vein stage almost always means losing the Responder.
category_qt_zombies_2: Never melee a Runner pack alone. Runners sprint faster than you can swing, and a single swipe can infect you. Either kite them into a chokepoint with gunfire or wait for a squadmate to lay down suppressive fire before closing the distance for a melee finisher.
category_weaknesses_guides: The biggest challenge with the guides category is that No More Room in Hell 2 changes often, and a guide written for one patch can quickly become out of date after a balance update. Zombie damage values, weapon recoil and infection stage timings are all subject to revision between major patches. New players can also feel overwhelmed by the sheer number of guides and overlapping systems, so we recommend reading them in order from Beginner through Advanced rather than jumping straight into Nightmare runs. Finally, no guide can replace actual squad play — the fastest way to learn the game is still to join a quiet server, deploy with three friends, and practice looting and extraction on a forgiving map like Lewiston before attempting the harder Raven Rock or Flooded maps.
category_weaknesses_maps: The biggest weakness of the maps category is that map layouts and objective sequences can change between patches, and any change to spawn points or wave triggers can invalidate a previously optimal route. We try to keep the map briefings current, but always verify the objectives against the in-game mission text before committing to a plan. Another challenge is that some maps depend heavily on squad size — Raven Rock is brutal with fewer than four players, while Lewiston can be solo'd by an experienced Responder on Normal difficulty. Treat the briefings as a starting point, not a script, and always adapt to your squad's actual composition.
category_weaknesses_multiplayer: The biggest weakness of the multiplayer category is that network performance varies by region and platform, so a setting that works perfectly for one player may not work for another. The Oceanic server was a recent addition, so Australian and New Zealand players still report higher ping than North American players on dedicated servers. Another challenge is that proximity voice chat can pick up background noise from squadmates who do not use push-to-talk, which sometimes forces squads to switch to Discord for cleaner communication. We try to keep the troubleshooting advice general, but always check the official Discord for the latest server status.
category_weaknesses_responders: The biggest weakness of the responders category is that roster management is highly personal — what works for a casual solo player (one Main + two Backups) is very different from what a hardcore co-op veteran needs (three rotating Mains with shared loadout caches). We give general recommendations, but you will need to adapt them to your own playstyle and squad composition. Another challenge is that some cosmetic unlocks and backgrounds are tied to specific Achievements or weekly Assignments, so a new player cannot immediately unlock the full roster of options.
category_weaknesses_skills: The biggest weakness of the skills category is that perk values change with every balance patch. The 1.0 Armageddon update rebalanced several perks, and any future balance pass could promote an underused perk to meta or knock an S-tier perk down a peg. We try to keep the values current, but always cross-check with the latest patch notes before committing Credits to a long perk chain. Another challenge is that perk value is highly dependent on squad composition — the Mule perk is amazing with three ammo-hungry rifle mains but useless for a stealth scout squad, and Acquired Immunity is mandatory on Nightmare but wasted on Beginner difficulty.
category_weaknesses_survival: The biggest weakness of the survival category is that infection timers and phalanx pill durations can change between patches. The 1.0 Armageddon update tweaked several survival values, and any future balance pass could shorten or extend the timer dramatically. Another challenge is that gene therapy vial spawn locations are fixed but randomised, so a guide can only tell you where to look, not where it will spawn on any given match. We recommend scouting the map before committing to an objective route so you know the candidate medical cabinet locations in advance.
category_weaknesses_tier-list: The biggest weakness of the tier list is that rankings depend on squad composition and difficulty — a weapon that is S-tier on Nightmare may be only A-tier on Normal, and a weapon that shines in a coordinated squad may be useless for a solo player. We try to call out the specific scenarios for each weapon, but always adapt the rankings to your own playstyle and squad size. Another challenge is that tier lists age quickly — a balance patch can promote an underused weapon to S tier overnight, so check the patch notes before committing Credits to a loadout based on the current rankings.
category_weaknesses_updates: The biggest weakness of the updates category is that patch notes are sometimes sparse — Torn Banner Studios occasionally drops a hotfix without a full changelog, so we have to infer the changes from community testing. Another challenge is that the wiki's build recommendations may lag a patch by a few days while we update perk values, weapon stats and tier lists. Always cross-check the latest patch notes with the wiki's tier list and meta-build guides before committing Credits to a loadout.
category_weaknesses_weapons: The biggest weakness of the weapons category is that No More Room in Hell 2 patches regularly change damage values, recoil and ammo weights. The Armageddon 1.0 update rebalanced several firearms, and any future balance pass could promote an underused weapon to S tier or knock an S-tier weapon down a peg. We try to keep the stats current, but always cross-check with the latest patch notes before committing Credits to an expensive loadout. Another challenge is that some weapons are situational — the sledgehammer is incredible for armored SWAT zombies but useless at range, and the MP5 is great for sustained close fire but weak against armored specials. Treat the tier list as a starting point, not a hard rule, and always weigh your squad composition and the map you are about to deploy into.
category_weaknesses_zombies: The main weakness of the zombies category is that spawn rates and zombie health values change with every balance patch. The 1.0 Armageddon update rebalanced several zombie types and added new themed variants, so any tier list written before 1.0 may already be slightly out of date. Another challenge is that zombie behaviour depends heavily on squad coordination — a coordinated squad with a designated Shambler-killer can ignore the tier list and farm Walkers forever, while a disorganised squad will be overwhelmed by Runners regardless of their stats. Treat the tier rankings as a guideline, not gospel, and always adapt to what you see on the map rather than what the wiki says you should see.

home_about_p1: No More Room in Hell 2 is a first-person cooperative zombie survival shooter from Torn Banner Studios, the team behind the original No More Room in Hell and Chivalry. Up to eight players drop into zombie-infested locations across the American Northeast Coast as volunteer Responders, completing missions for the Civil Recovery Corps while scavenging gear and fighting for their lives.
home_about_p2: Every run is high-stakes — a single infection can turn your character against the squad, and true permadeath means a fallen Responder is gone for good. Between deployments you invest Credits earned from extracted supplies into new skills, loadouts and cosmetic upgrades back at your campsite. The Armageddon 1.0 update launched the game on consoles with Survival mode, solo play and the new Raven Rock map.
home_about_title: What is No More Room in Hell 2?
home_cta_description: Arm your Responder, learn the horde, and complete your first extraction. Our guides cover everything from first deployment to Nightmare runs.
home_faq_bestWeapons_a: The Fierra DB12 shotgun and M7A1 carbine dominate most encounters thanks to high per-shot damage and controllable spread. For solo play the M1911 pistol is reliable, and the Rochester 1873 revolver and sledgehammer are excellent melee swaps. Check the full weapon tier list for the latest Armageddon 1.0 balance rankings.
home_faq_bestWeapons_q: What are the best weapons in No More Room in Hell 2?
home_faq_difficultyLevels_a: The game offers Beginner, Normal, Hard and Nightmare. Higher difficulties raise zombie damage, spawn density and the chance of infection, but they also multiply the Credits you earn from extracted supplies. Most responders grind Hard for steady progression and only attempt Nightmare runs with a coordinated veteran squad.
home_faq_difficultyLevels_q: What difficulty levels are available in No More Room in Hell 2?
home_faq_howManyPlayers_a: Up to 8 players per squad across PC, PS5 and Xbox via full crossplay. You can play solo as well, especially with the Solo mode added in 1.0 Armageddon, but the game is built around coordinated squad play with proximity voice chat rewarding teams that stick together.
home_faq_howManyPlayers_q: How many players can play No More Room in Hell 2 together?
home_faq_howToPlay_a: Buy it on Steam, PS5 or Xbox, then create your first Responder at the campsite. Pick a starting loadout from your Credits budget and join a public or friends-only lobby to begin your first deployment. The objective is to scavenge supplies, complete mission goals and extract before your character is overwhelmed by the horde.
home_faq_howToPlay_q: How do I start playing No More Room in Hell 2?
home_faq_infectionCure_a: Yes — phalanx pills buy time by slowing the infection progression for one bottle (3 doses total). The real cure is the gene therapy vial, of which exactly one spawns per match. Find it and administer it to a fully-infected teammate for a full reversal and immunity for the rest of the deployment.
home_faq_infectionCure_q: Can you cure NPV infection in No More Room in Hell 2?
home_faq_isPermadeath_a: Yes — when a Responder dies or fully converts from NPV infection, that character is gone for good and any unspent XP or credits are lost. That is why the campsite lets you keep up to three Responders active at once, so you always have a backup plan when one of your squadmates takes a fatal hit on Nightmare difficulty.
home_faq_isPermadeath_q: Is permadeath really permanent in No More Room in Hell 2?
home_faq_platforms_a: Yes — the Armageddon 1.0 update on August 11 2026 brought the full game to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, joining the existing Steam and Epic Games Store PC versions. Crossplay is enabled by default, so a PC squad and a console squad can deploy together in the same lobby.

weapon_m1911_damage: Three-tap Walkers at close range, two-tap headshots, decent penetration

zombie_crawler_counter: Stomp or melee before walking over, never ignore
zombie_crawler_threat: Low — dismembered Runner, cannot chase but can grab and infect
zombie_prime_runner_counter: Armor-piercing rifle or shotgun slug to the head
zombie_prime_runner_threat: Extreme — combines Runner speed with armor and huge health pool
zombie_runner_counter: Headshots from any rifle, kite into chokepoints
zombie_runner_threat: High — sprints in short bursts and flanks in narrow corridors
zombie_shambler_counter: Shotgun slug or rifle headshot from distance, never melee
zombie_shambler_threat: High — emits toxic gas and a scream that summons Runner waves
zombie_walker_counter: Melee or single-shot headshots, ignore when busy
zombie_walker_threat: Low — slow shambling horde, easiest target to conserve ammo
